title: 8670 Prerequisite Review — Fundamentals of National Defense
notice: Five demonstration questions derived from Lesson 2 Reading, Fundamentals of National Defense, in the AY27 8670 Prerequisite Coursebook. Source page numbers refer to the original 220-page Moodle PDF.

questions.prompt: In the coursebook’s ends–ways–means framework, what are ‘ways’?

options.a: The resources available to execute a strategy
options.b: The objectives the strategy seeks to achieve
options.c: The methods used to employ resources toward objectives
options.d: The risks resulting from an unbalanced strategy

questions.source_ref: AY27 8670 Prerequisite Coursebook — Lesson 2 Reading: Fundamentals of National Defense, §2.c (Strategy Theory), PDF p. 5 of 220.

questions.prompt: A national strategy uses trade regulation, loans, and foreign aid to pursue its objectives. Which instrument of national power is primarily involved?
questions.source_ref: AY27 8670 Prerequisite Coursebook — Lesson 2 Reading: Fundamentals of National Defense, §2.d(4) (Economic), PDF p. 6 of 220.

questions.prompt: A credible threat of unacceptable counteraction prevents an adversary from taking an undesired action. Which strategic use of military force does this describe?
questions.source_ref: AY27 8670 Prerequisite Coursebook — Lesson 2 Reading: Fundamentals of National Defense, §3.a(2) (Deterrence), PDF p. 13 of 220.

questions.prompt: Which statement best reflects the coursebook’s distinction between war’s nature and its character?

options.a: War’s nature changes with technology, while its character remains fixed.
options.b: War’s nature remains fundamentally human, while its character reflects changing societal and technological conditions.
options.c: War’s nature consists of its equipment, while its character consists only of human emotions.
options.d: Both war’s nature and character remain unchanged across time and societies.

questions.source_ref: AY27 8670 Prerequisite Coursebook — Lesson 2 Reading: Fundamentals of National Defense, §4.a–b (The Nature of War; Changing Character of War), PDF pp. 15–16 of 220.

questions.prompt: Which activity best exemplifies the operational level of war?

options.c: Linking tactical results through a campaign to achieve strategic objectives
options.d: Coordinating all instruments of national power into national strategy

questions.source_ref: AY27 8670 Prerequisite Coursebook — Lesson 2 Reading: Fundamentals of National Defense, §4.d(3) (Operational Level), PDF p. 18 of 220.
